transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-07
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Samir (Valencia CTO), Lena (Head of Data), Priya (Retail Ops)

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focusing on per-route analytics and cost. Customer wants to understand hot paths, token costs, and how canary rollouts would affect peak latency.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE for Valencia. Ethan's going to do most of the console walkthrough. Quick intros?
[00:12] Samir: Samir here, CTO. We run recommender and a shopper assist chat across web and mobile. We're trying to get a handle on cost at peak and latency for checkout flows.
[00:25] Lena: Hi I'm Lena, Head of Data, I'll be owners for telemetry and evals.
[00:30] Priya: Priya, ops -- interested in outage behaviours and SLA.
[00:35] Ethan: Cool thanks. I'll share my screen, give a tour of Console: usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown. Note: deck and benchmark sheet will be posted after.

[01:10] Ethan: (screen) starting at the Usage page, you can see token consumption trends by day, the per-route breakdown on the right — this is where most teams start. We also surface tail latency percentiles and SLO alerts.
[01:30] Samir: That per-route view, is that per-endpoint or per-intent? We have both a chat endpoint and a batch async embedding job.
[01:40] Ethan: Good q. It's by route name, which you can map to endpoints or intents. Many customers create a route per product flow, e.g., /chat/assist-checkout, /embed-batch-pricing.
[01:58] Ethan: You can filter by model version, region, and deployment type (hosted vs dedicated).

[02:20] Lena: How accurate are the token counts? We saw mismatches in another tool where special chars blew up counts.
[02:28] Ethan: We use tokenization close to the model's tokenizer; there can be off-by-one in weird utf cases. We report both raw tokens and billed tokens so you can reconcile.

[03:05] Ethan: Moving to per-route dashboard — this shows throughput, p50/p90/p99 latencies, and cost per 1k requests. The cost calc is token-level + compute amortized. It's an estimate but maps closely to invoicing.
[03:30] Maya: Worth noting we give suggestions under Optimize — e.g., batch config, KV cache suggestions, quantization proposals for heavy routes.

[04:00] Samir: Can we see an example for checkout flow? That's our tightest SLO at p95 < 300ms.
[04:12] Ethan: Sure, switching to route /chat/assist-checkout. You can see p50 ~120ms, p95 290ms (on weekdays peak). The platform shows spikes where fallback to hosted variants occurred.
[04:35] Priya: Fallback? explain that.
[04:38] Ethan: If dedicated capacity is saturated we automatically route to compatible hosted variants per your policy. We show those events in the trace timeline. We also have canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies if a new model degrades latency.

[05:10] Lena: For the p95 290ms, is that including network egress to our VPC? We plan a VPC deployment.
[05:20] Ethan: The Console latency includes server-side processing. If you're on Private (VPC) there's an extra network hop; in Private mode we show separate metrics you can correlate with your infra traces.

[06:00] Ethan: Now cost breakdown — here's token-level cost per route. You can break down prompt vs completion tokens, model family, and storage (KV cache) costs.
[06:25] Samir: How do you recommend lowering unit cost without breaking latency?
[06:30] Ethan: A few levers: batching for background routes (embeddings), prefix caching/KV cache for chat to avoid re-generation, using quantized/dedicated model variants for heavy synchronous routes, and smart routing — send low-priority traffic to cheaper regions.
[06:50] Maya: We also provide per-route suggestions in Optimize which rank suggested changes by estimated cost reduction and risk to latency.

[07:20] Lena: We have multi-tenant traffic — need token-level breakout by user cohort. Is that supported?
[07:28] Ethan: We surface per-route and per-api-key metrics. Many customers create per-cohort api-keys to get that slice. We also export full events to your data lake if you want joinable telemetry.

[08:10] Samir: Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS? We have strict audit needs.
[08:18] Maya: We have SOC2 Type II (link), detailed audit logs in the Console, SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC at team/route level, and KMS integrations for Private deployments.
[08:35] Samir: For Private on-prem, does Redwood manage the control plane?
[08:40] Ethan: In Private we give you a customer-managed control plane option; there's an on-prem package for air-gapped. Key material can live in your HSM/KMS.

[09:05] Priya: What about data residency? We need EU-only for some flows.
[09:12] Ethan: You can pin routes to regions; we support region-locked deployments and audit logs for residency proofs.

[10:00] Ethan: Back to cost — here's a simulated cost-saver view: enabling prefix cache reduced token generation by ~22% in one case. We show estimated monthly savings and confidence band.
[10:25] Lena: That confidence band, is it from actual runs or modelling?
[10:30] Ethan: A mix — historical run data + model of usage patterns. For new routes it's primarily modeled until we have a week's traffic.

[11:05] Samir: On dedicated vs hosted: what's the typical commit for a mid-market retailer?
[11:12] Maya: Typical reserved committed capacity for someone your size is 2-6 GPUs equivalent with burst options; we can sketch numbers in the pricing doc.
[11:25] Samir: And auto-scaling? we have big flash sales.
[11:28] Ethan: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity to handle spikes with minimal latency impact. The Console surfaces utilization and predicted headroom.

[12:00] Priya: If we do a POC, can we run load with our replay traffic and get the same Console dashboards?
[12:08] Ethan: Yes — we provide a benchmark template and you'll see the same metrics. We can also run a side-by-side cost comparison in the sheet.

[13:00] (minor crosstalk)
[13:20] Samir: One concern: tokenization differences across models. We use long prompts, can that swing cost?
[13:30] Ethan: Absolutely — tokenization matters. We recommend tests with representative prompts. Also Optimize may propose a shorter system prompt or structured output to cut tokens.

[14:10] Lena: Are there alerts when route cost crosses a threshold?
[14:15] Ethan: Yep — you can set budget alerts per route with email/Slack hooks and automatic throttling or fallback policies.

[15:05] Maya: Quick demo of a per-route trace — you can click an individual request, see the token breakdown, model variant used, and the fallback history.
[15:25] Ethan: Here's an example trace where p99 spikes — we can see a batch job contending with sync requests and the batch was deprioritized.

[16:00] Samir: Do you support function calls / tooling? We have a middleware that calls inventory API.
[16:08] Ethan: Yes — Console captures function/tool call counts and the extra latency. We also show cost of external tool calls if proxied through our runtime.

[17:00] Priya: For the SLOs, can Redwood automatically rollback a deploy that increases latency?
[17:07] Ethan: Yes — we support canary rollouts and automatic rollback policies when latency or error-rate regressions pass thresholds.

[18:30] Samir: Any gotchas for our stack? We use client-side batching in the browser for suggestions.
[18:38] Ethan: Browser batching can help, but watch cold starts for KV cache. Also ensure short-lived API keys rotate regularly — our Console helps manage keys.

[20:00] (screen moves to Pricing estimator)
[20:10] Ethan: This estimator simulates cost given traffic, model choice, and routing policies. You can toggle dedicated vs hosted and see monthly delta.
[20:30] Maya: We'll include a conservative baseline and a dedicated commit option in the follow-up pricing.

[22:00] Lena: If we go dedicated, will we lose visibility into per-route cost?
[22:06] Ethan: No — Console unifies metrics across hosted/dedicated/private. Cost attribution is shown even for dedicated (we amortize infra).

[23:20] Samir: About integrations: we use Datadog and Splunk. Can we export traces?
[23:28] Ethan: Yep — event and trace exports via Kafka/S3 and Datadog/Splunk hooks.

[25:00] (brief pause)
[25:20] Priya: SLAs and penalties?
[25:25] Maya: Enterprise SLAs exist on Dedicated; details in the contract. We'll share the SLA appendix.

[26:40] Ethan: Walkthrough wrap-up: key places to look in Console — Usage > Per-route > Optimize suggestions > Traces > Export.
[27:05] Samir: Ok really helpful. For the POC we want a 1-week run using our replay, and a cost report comparing hosted vs 3-GPU dedicated.
[27:18] Maya: Great, we'll send pricing and the benchmark template.

[28:00] Lena: We might want to test quantized variants for checkout only — any risk?
[28:08] Ethan: Quantization can slightly change output quality; Optimize includes a regression alert on eval prompts. We recommend canary on a small cohort first.

[30:00] Samir: Competitors — we compared to OpenAI and Anthropic; what's your differentiation on visibility?
[30:08] Maya: Our focus is production-grade visibility and cost controls: token-level, per-route recommendations, and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private.

[31:10] Priya: One question on billing granularity: can we get per-route invoice lines for chargeback?
[31:20] Ethan: Yes, we support per-route or per-api-key billing exports for internal chargeback.

[33:00] (Ethan shares link to benchmark sheet)
[33:10] Ethan: Link: (benchmark-sheet) — we'll populate with your traffic patterns once you share.

[34:00] Samir: We'll aim to share sample traffic and a SLO doc by end of week.
[34:08] Maya: Noted — Samir will own that.

[35:00] (small interruptions, some audio artifacts)
[36:20] Priya: A final ops Q: how long until observability retention increases cost?
[36:28] Ethan: Longer retention increases storage costs; we can tier retention per route or export to your lake for long-term.

[38:00] Maya: Okay summarizing: Maya to send pricing and reserved commit options; Ethan to share benchmark template and run initial cost calc; Samir to provide traffic and SLOs. Schedule POC start for next week pending data.
[38:25] Samir: Sounds good.
[39:10] Lena: Please include the SOC2 link and data flow diagram in the docs.
[39:18] Maya: Will do.
[40:30] Priya: Thanks all.
[40:35] Ethan: Thanks, we'll follow up with links and the POC plan.
[41:00] (meeting ends)
